IN DEPTH:
BEYOND FUTILE NEGOTIATIONS AND SELF-DELUDING DIPLOMACY: AGREEMENTS WITH THE MENDACIOUS PUTIN ARE WORTHLESS AND HARMFUL; US MUST HELP UKRAINE TO PREVAIL!

The duplicitous and untrustworthy characters of both Alaska summiteers Putin and Trump are making the whole idea of negotiations and security guarantees virtually worthless. What good can a treaty or other international agreement with Putin be, given his obsessive habit of violating all such "deals." The same goes for the erratic and labile Trump, who has shifted his entire Ukraine policy several times in the last few weeks.

THE GROMOV PLAN FOR AFGHANISTAN, 1989

Fortunately, not all wars end in negotiations, whatever ignorant journalists may parrot about this matter. For the most obvious example, let us look at Russia's last major foreign war, which was in Afghanistan between 1979 and 1989. There were virtually no international negotiations about the end of that war. Once the Soviet Union had recognized its own defeat, the Gorbachev regime simply decided to bring its invaders home. In 1989, Gen. Boris Gromov became famous for leading his troops back across a bridge from Afghanistan into Soviet Uzbekistan. With that, the war was over.

If Putin really wanted peace, he could ask Gromov, who is still alive and well and living in Moscow. The secret will turn out to be: find the nearest Russian border and march your troops back across that border. Q.E.D.!

The biggest single factor in the Soviet decision to end the aggression and bring the Red Army home from Afghanistan had absolute nothing to do with diplomacy or negotiations. It was rather a matter of unsustainable losses inflicted by US weaponry.

The main factor for peace was the timely delivery, free gratis, of superior American technology in the form of Stinger anti-aircraft missiles and related MANPADS to vanquish the feared Soviet Hind helicopters and other warplanes. Movie-goers know this story from the 2007 Hollywood hit "Charley Wilson's War." This suggests the US-NATO way out of the Ukraine crisis: the massive delivery of the most modern US weapons to drive the Russians out.

THE 1985 REAGAN DOCTRINE

This outlook gave rise to the Reagan Doctrine, which moved US policy away from detente and containment towards rollback of Soviet aggression. As Reagan stated in his 1985 State of the Union address: 

"We must not break faith with those who are risking their lives—on every continent from Afghanistan to Nicaragua—to defy Soviet-supported aggression and secure rights which have been ours from birth." 

Transpose this to present-day Ukraine, and it must be required reading for Trump today.

Back in the 1930s, it only gradually became clear that negotiations and treaties with the Nazi regime in Germany were useless and actually harmful. Hitler violated the Versailles Treaty by reintroducing German troops into the demilitarized Rhineland in a 1936. In 1938, he violated Versailles and the 1925 Locarno Pact by merging Austria back into Germany--the Anschluss which these treaties had forbidden.

Later in 1938, Hitler demanded the Sudetenland area of Czechoslovakia, which was given to him by Britain and France at the high point of appeasement at the September 1938 Munich conference. Hitler kept saying that this was his last territorial demand in Europe. But by March 1939, Hitler had gobbled up whatever was left of Czechoslovakia.

In the summer of 1939, Hitler began demanding the city of Danzig/Gdansk and the Polish corridor door, which had been assigned to the newly re-created Poland at Versailles. Only after Hitler attacked Poland on September 1, 1939, Britain and France finally declared war on Germany, starting World War Two in Europe. Even then, the UK and France did almost nothing to help Poland. The phony war in the west lasted until the spring of 1940. The appeasement habit proved very hard to break.

The lesson: when dealing with unprincipled, fanatic, aggressive, dictators like Putin, there comes a point after which the formalities of diplomacy and negotiations become a form of self-delusion. A good guess is that this point was passed no later than last week at the failed Alaska appeasement summit. This quick review of some relevant historical points suggests that the way to end the Ukraine war is for the United States to generously arm Ukraine with the most modern weaponry, to provide a solid logistical backup with the sinews of war, to weaken the Russian economy still further by more severe economic sanctions, to extend secondary sanctions to dissuade China, India, and others from financing Russia's war with their oil purchases, and to seize Russian assets held in the West, delivering the proceeds to Ukraine to defray the cost of defeating the Russian aggression. This is the path to peace.

It should also be clear that the implementation of Trump's obvious appeasement and sellout designs would represent an engraved invitation for a Chinese attack on Taiwan. In this sense, today's White House gathering should include Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the Philippines, and Australia in addition to the Europeans. Ukraine is a vital issue for the Indo-Pacific as well.

THE FOLLY OF APPEASEMENT

As Gen. Douglas MacArthur told a Joint Session of Congress in April 1951:

"...once war is forced upon us, there is no other alternative than to apply every available means to bring it to a swift end. War's very object is victory, not prolonged indecision. 

"In war, there is no substitute for victory. 

"There are some who, for varying reasons, would appease Red China. They are blind to history's clear lesson, for history teaches with unmistakable emphasis that appeasement but begets new and bloodier war. It points to no single instance where this end has justified that means, where appeasement has led to more than a sham peace. Like blackmail, it lays the basis for new and successively greater demands until, as in blackmail, violence becomes the only other alternative."
